note: The two sets are nearly identical in content; the only differences are in the Young's modulus and shear modulus of steel claims, where A binds the values to 'tower steel' and keeps the Table 4-1 condition while B uses the vaguer entity 'steel' and drops the condition. Both sets share the same weaknesses: three overlapping claims about the tower's first natural frequency (0.18 Hz, 0.17 Hz, 0.170 Hz), one of which (0.18 Hz) contradicts the stated 0.170 Hz. A is marginally more precise and faithful, so it is the better set.
remarks: Both sets report the tower 1st natural frequency three times (0.18 Hz, 0.17 Hz, 0.170 Hz); the 0.18 Hz value contradicts the text's 0.170 Hz and appears to be a misread of the figure line. The 1P (0.09-0.13 Hz) and 3P (0.25-0.38 Hz) ranges and the wave-spectrum peak at 0.11 Hz are read off Figure 4-1 and are approximate but plausible. Important facts both sets omit: the 7% outfitting mass allowance, the 100 t transition piece mass, the requirement for a stiffer tower with a floating/semisubmersible substructure, and the soil being modeled with spring constants representative of dense sand or gravel.
